test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following national income aggregates is generally recognised as National Income of a country?

options.text: Net National Product at Market Prices
Net National Product at Factor Cost
Gross National Product at Market Prices
Gross Domestic Product at Factor Cost

solution:
The correct answer is __**Net National Product at Factor Cost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost, also referred to as National Income, is the aggregate value of all goods and services produced within a country after accounting for depreciation and taxes.
 
• It is derived by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from Gross National Product (GNP) at Factor Cost.
 
• Unlike market prices, factor cost excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies, making it a more accurate measure of the income earned by factors of production.
 
• NNP at Factor Cost is widely used by governments and economists to assess the economic performance and income distribution of a nation.
 
• This measurement reflects the total earnings of a country's residents from the production of goods and services during a specific time period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP):**

 
 
• GNP refers to the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents in a given period, regardless of where the production takes place.
 
• It includes income earned by nationals working abroad but excludes income earned by foreigners within the country.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP):**
 
 
• NNP is GNP adjusted for depreciation, which accounts for the wear and tear of capital assets used in production.
 
• It represents the actual addition to a country's stock of wealth during a year.
 
 
 
• **Factor Cost vs. Market Prices:**
 
 
• Factor Cost accounts for the cost of production, including wages, rent, interest, and profits, but excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies.
 
• Market Prices, on the other hand, include indirect taxes and exclude subsidies, reflecting the price paid by consumers.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation:**
 
 
• Depreciation, also known as consumption of fixed capital, refers to the reduction in the value of assets due to wear and tear over time.
 
• It is subtracted from GNP to calculate NNP.
 
 
 
• **Importance of NNP at Factor Cost:**
 
 
• It serves as a comprehensive indicator of a nation's economic health and income distribution.
 
• It helps policymakers in planning and implementing economic policies aimed at improving living standards.
